claims.plain: The arcuate body is built from four sublayers, and each neurotransmitter population innervates its own subset of them.
Staining several neurotransmitters at once separates arcuate body layers that synapsin staining alone leaves indistinct.
Every claim here is an anatomical observation read off the atlas volumes rather than a statistical test.
Serotonin and octopamine/tyramine fibres fill the cheliceral neuropil most heavily and continue just medial to it.
The anti-GAD antibody stains only the outer edge of the whole-mount, so GABA patterns in the deeper neuropils cannot be trusted.
The globuli cells at the mushroom body heads stain for ChAT and, more weakly, GAD, marking them as cholinergic and GABAergic.
Serotonin completely fills the newly named hagstone neuropil, and its staining is what marks the structure's boundaries.
Serotonin fibres reach each leg neuropil from the dorsal-most tract and fill it as two equal halves around a central void.
All four pairs of leg neuropils carry the same innervation pattern for every neurotransmitter mapped.
Uloborus diversus, a web-building spider, has complete mushroom bodies, and only allatostatin A is found throughout them.
Octopamine/tyramine fibres ring the edge of the opisthosomal neuropil and form a ladder of crossing projections toward its back.
Acetylcholine and octopamine/tyramine stain most strongly in the pedipalpal neuropil, and neither reaches its front portion.
The spider brain contains a protocerebral bridge, a candidate counterpart of the insect central complex used in path integration.
The protocerebral bridge is layered by transmitter, with GABA spanning it and octopamine, proctolin and acetylcholine in bands.
A previously undescribed neuropil, named the tonsillar neuropil, stands out in the spider synganglion by its staining pattern.
Serotonin fills the tonsillar neuropil's core, octopamine/tyramine forms a shell around it, and two peptides sit only at its rear.
A three-dimensional atlas places GABA, acetylcholine, serotonin, octopamine and several peptides in the spider's neuropils.
